body:
N-48 CORRECTION to the two result notes of 26 Nov 2026 (lead, after the advisor's read; THESE NUMBERS REPLACE THE EARLIER ONES).

(1) THE STRICT JUDGE NEVER RAN in the first report: the tool fed mapped album tracks to album_finder.judge_hits, which reads raw catalogue rows, so every row came back unreadable and 'strict' was ISRC-equal only (the tell: 'carrier found only by name: 0 of 47'). Fixed in n48_measure.py: the same artist+title+version key test at the matcher's 3 s and at the loose 20 s.

(2) THE FROZEN RULE (what a build must implement, nothing looser): the recording is carried by exactly ONE release family under the strict 3 s AND the loose 20 s (a carrier is an ISRC-equal track or the same artist, title and version key within the tolerance; a release counts only if the matcher's own _why_not lets it and its title is no compilation); abstain on a cut release list, a track list at the 100 limit, an artist with no releases, an album that could not be asked; NO by_share, NO single stamp, NO year. Under it: 63 of the 135 held songs get a home (NOT 74): date_decided 3 of 24, single_before_album 20 of 27, sole_album 37 of 49, single_only 3 of 32, compilation_title 0 of 3. 58 name the album the matcher had picked, 5 name another: Hotel -> Split Personality, Break Stuff -> Significant Other, Reptilia -> Room on Fire are right (the lead's own knowledge, no source consulted); Love Ghost 'Thirteen' and Suzi Wu 'Error 404' are UNVERIFIED. The earlier '7 right as far as read' overstated: Misery Business, I Bet You Look Good On The Dancefloor and What's My Age Again? are name-only carriers that the strict 3 s now holds back (3 songs where strict and loose disagree stay held).

(3) Labeled set of 11 under the frozen rule: 0 wrong, 4 right (T-Pain, Hotel, Outkast, Limp Bizkit), 7 abstain (Ja Rule, three Linkin Park, MCR, Fat Joe, blink-182 'All The Small Things': it was a by_share answer). The 41 good stamps: 38 agree, 3 abstain, 0 contradict.

(4) Name-only carriers among the 63: ONE (Hotel: the song's ISRC differs from the 2024 re-release's track). A name-only carrier may decide the album but must write NO ISRC and NO deezer_id.

(5) IN-SAMPLE: the rule was changed twice on these 176 songs (the loose 20 s after MCR, dropping by_share after Spiderbait); 'zero wrong' is not independent evidence. The build's acceptance is a fresh dry run over songs the rule was NOT shaped on, every answer read.

(6) single_only with no home: 27; 3 of them are dated in the last 18 months (all three in Oct 2026, very recent singles whose album may still come): the single-stamp question stays closed (N-51). YEAR restated on the 101 songs that have an ISRC year and a real date: the ISRC year equals the date's year in 63, is within one year in 83, and the date is a reissue (more than a year later) in 15. Ruling stands: NO year (N-50, later).

The texts in PR #135 (comments, docs/18, the design doc, the N-48 item note) say 74; they are corrected to 63 in the next PR.
